Wicklow County Council launches €646,000 Community Climate Action Programme 
Wicklow County Council has announced the launch of the second round of the Community Climate Action 
Programme, offering €646,000 in funding to assist community, voluntary, and non-profit groups in 
delivering local climate and biodiversity projects across the county.  
This new round of funding, supported by the Department of Climate, Energy, and the Environment, will 
provide grants of up to €100,000 per project to support local climate actions aimed at reducing carbon 
emissions, enhancing biodiversity and building community resilience.  
Following the success of the first round, where 19 community groups in Wicklow implemented projects 
including solar panel installations, energy efficiency upgrades, bike facilities and biodiversity initiatives, 
this new programme will continue to empower local communities to take meaningful climate action.  
 
Wicklow County Council welcomes Delegation from Netherlands 
Wicklow County Council's Town Regeneration Office recently welcomed a delegation from Heerlen, 
Netherlands, as part of the EU City-to-City Exchange programme. This initiative aims to foster 
collaboration, share best practices and explore innovative approaches to town regeneration.  
The visit, hosted by Wicklow County Council, focused on showcasing recent developments in town centre 
revitalisation across the county. The Heerlen delegation met with elected officials, town teams and 
community organisations to discuss strategies for creating vibrant, resilient and inclusive town centres.  
During the visit, participants explored key regeneration projects in Wicklow Town and 
Newtownmountkennedy, highlighting initiatives that balance heritage preservation with modern urban 
needs. Discussions centred on common challenges faced by towns in both County Wicklow and the 
Netherlands, including vacant properties, changing retail consumer behaviour, sustainable mobility and 
community engagement.  
The Heerlen delegation shared insights from their successful transformation strategies, including 
innovative approaches to reusing vacant properties, supporting local enterprises, fostering cultural 
vibrancy and promoting active involvement of young people in shaping the future of their towns and cities. 
Both sides agreed that ongoing collaboration could help identify practical solutions to the challenges of 
town centre renewal.

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units. Eleven families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning to a 
permanent home and the resulting vacancies are in the process of being occupied with families 
experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully 
operational. Wicklow County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they 
continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
 
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing 
Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support 
needs of the clients. Six of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved 
into their forever homes and this in turn created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful.

Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme Update: Wicklow County Council  
The Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme in Wicklow continues to support older people, over 65 years 
of age, to live in their home for as long as possible.  
The Programme accepts referrals from a variety of sources including from: 
- 
The older person themselves 
- Local Authority Staff 
- 
Family and friends 
 
- Public Health Nurses, GP’s and Occupational Therapists   
- 
Elected Representatives 
- Community Organisations 
 
Please note, consent from the older person (verbal) must be obtained before the referral is submitted. 
Once the referral is received, the Local Coordinator will be in-touch with the older person to arrange a 
free home visit.   
 
Referrals to the programme can be made via phone or email: 
046-924 8899 (Head Office)  
 
 
 
 healthyagefriendlyhomes@meathcoco.ie 
 
Since the commencement of the Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme in Wicklow, in January 2024, 
the level of interest in the programme has been greater than anticipated. Consequently, a large number of 
referrals to the programme in Wicklow have been received, and the wait times to be seen by the Local 
Coordinator are longer than originally forecast. 
Since her appointment to her role in January, Local Coordinator for Wicklow, Marion Van der Wel, has been 
conducting home assessments on a weekly basis to our programme participants. As part of her role, Marion 
offers a wide range of supports to our participants, including but not limited to, arranging fall detector 
personal alarms, helping with housing adaptation grants, organising Care and Repair services, linking-in 
with community services, signposting the older person to health services etc.  
 
The programme has gone from strength-to-strength in Wicklow since its inception. The 2024 projected 
targets for the programme in Wicklow have been exceeded, which demonstrates the success of the 
programme, and is a testament to the concerted collaborative efforts of the Local Coordinator and Local 
Authority Staff. 
 
Referrals to Healthy Age Friendly Homes Programme:  
After a concerted level of stakeholder engagement and programme promotion early in 2024, the number of 
referrals to the programme in Wicklow reached peak demand. A decision was then made to curtail 
programme promotion in order to stabilise programme demand. Consequently, demand for the programme 
in Wicklow has stabilised in recent months, and more sustainable pattern of referrals are now emerging.

Blessington, as a Pathfinder Town, was selected as the first town in Co. Wicklow to develop a Town Centre 
First (TCF) Masterplan. This masterplan, published in 2023, offers a clear and strategic framework for the 
town’s positive and sustainable development of the town, both in the short term and in the future, with a 
strong focus on community well-being, economic resilience, and placemaking.

Newtownmountkennedy was one of 26 towns selected nationally under Phase 2 of the Town Centre First

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant. 
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Information Systems 
 
Operations  
 
• 
The IT Helpdesk continues to streamline the workflow for the technical support team with an average of 50 tickets 
a day this month, providing assistance for both in-house and remote workers.  
 
GIS & Systems Analysis 
• 
Sustainable Communities Report – Blessington 
Work was completed on a series of maps showing the range of services available in Blessington, including 
schools, health services, transport links, and recreational facilities. These maps will help provide a clear picture 
of community needs and support future planning. The information forms part of the wider Sustainable 
Communities Report. 
 
• 
Residential and Population Analysis 
A detailed review of housing and population targets was carried out across all county settlements. This helps to 
create a reliable baseline for planning future housing needs. The work ensures that development is balanced 
and aligned with community requirements. 
 
• 
Arklow Local Area Plan Consultation Hub 
The new online Consultation Hub for the Arklow Local Area Plan has gone live. This platform makes it easier for 
the public to engage with the planning process and share feedback. Automated tools are in place to ensure 
responses are gathered efficiently and reported accurately. 
 
• 
Environment GIS 
Flood zoning maps were updated using the latest datasets from the County Development Plan. These updates 
improve the accuracy of flood risk mapping. The information will support environmental assessments and 
responsible development decisions. 
 
• 
Fire Service Planning 
Work is underway to carry out a population density study for each fire station in the county. This will help ensure 
that fire services are well matched to local needs. The study will also compare fire station boundaries with 
national population data to highlight any service gaps. 
 
Infrastructure 
• 
Ongoing upgrades of WAN connections at remote sites by Wicklow County Council aim to optimize performance 
and cost-effectiveness.
